The data is the bundled 'edge-cases' dataset, reproduced here in full; no network access is needed. Raw papers, keywords exactly as extracted: E1: ['--', 'Large-Language Model', 'large language model', 'LARGE_LANGUAGE/MODEL', 'LLMs']; E2: []; E3: ['+++']; E4: ['NMT', 'GPT']; E5: ['News', 'Bias', 'Gender Bias']; E6: ['Sentiment Analysis', 'Parallel Corpus', 'Word Class', 'Case Studies', 'Ties']; E9: ['GANs', 'Nets', 'Gas']; E10: ['Q&A', 'Word Vectors', 'Word Embeddings', 'Graphs Neural Network']. Alias table, already in normalized form, alias -> canonical: bias -> bias; decoder only transformer -> decoder only model; gan -> generative adversarial network; generative pretrained transformer -> decoder only transformer; gpt -> generative pretrained transformer; llm -> large language model; neural machine translation -> machine translation; news -> news; nmt -> neural machine translation; qa -> question answering; word vectors -> word embeddings. A key mapped to itself ('bias', 'news') marks a protected word.

For each raw keyword apply, in order: N1 lowercase it; N2 turn each '-', '_' and '/' into a space; N3 delete every character that is not a-z, 0-9 or a space; N4 collapse runs of spaces and strip leading and trailing spaces; N5 drop the keyword if nothing survives ('--' and '+++' contribute nothing). A1: if the normalized form is an alias key, replace it with its canonical form and keep replacing while the new form is also a key mapping to something different (chains are followed; a self-mapped key stops the chain). A2: if A1 applied, or the keyword is a self-mapped key, the result is final and plural stripping is skipped. Only when strip_plurals is true (as in this task) and A1 did not apply, apply P1 to the keyword's last word only (the text after its last space, or the whole keyword when it has no space); all other words stay exactly as they are. P1 on that last word: if it ends in 'ies', replace 'ies' with 'y' only when it is longer than 4 letters, otherwise leave it unchanged ('ties' stays 'ties'); if it ends in 'ss', 'us' or 'is', leave it; otherwise if it ends in 's' and is longer than 3 letters, remove the final 's'. Then P2: look the whole singularized keyword up in the alias table and resolve it as in A1; if it is not a key, the singularized form is final (so a plural form whose singular is an alias key reaches the alias's value). Protection covers whole keywords only: a protected word keeps its own form but does not protect the same word as the last word of a longer keyword. An alias result is final even when it ends in 's', so a keyword that resolved through an alias is never plural-stripped.

Per paper, collect all final forms, remove duplicates, and sort ascending. Papers with no keywords, or none surviving normalization (E2; E3), still appear, with an empty concepts list. The output echoes the input's dataset and strip_plurals unchanged, and lists every paper exactly once, sorted by paper_id in Python's default string order, so the order is E1, E10, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6, E9 (string order puts E10 before E2). Each concept must be a non-empty run of a-z and 0-9 words joined by single spaces.
